nodes.description: Not tested in patients or in an animal model of the disease. It has been proposed on the haploinsufficiency model, and the TOPORS coding sequence fits within the capacity of an AAV vector. If the dominant-negative model is correct, adding a normal copy may not be sufficient.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in the dominantly inherited TOPORS gene supports haploinsufficiency as the mechanism of retinitis pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: Since the cDNA encoding TOPORS is 3,135 nucleotides (within the coding capacity of AAV vectors) and haploinsufficiency is a mechanism relating to inadequate gene expression, gene replacement therapy may be an option for patients with this condition.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a heterozygous germline TOPORS variant. Most are frameshift or nonsense variants in the last exon (exon 3) that fall between residues 807 and 867, near the C-terminus of the 1,045 residue protein; truncating variants outside this window, and N-terminal copy number losses, are found in people without RP. Missense variants make up about a third of reported alleles and include p.Gln402Pro, which causes a pericentral form.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Retinitis Pigmentosa-Associated TOPORS Protein Truncating Variants Are Exclusively Located in the Region of Amino Acid Residues 807 to 867.
evidence.snippet: All RP-associated truncating alleles, except one, were distributed in the last exon of TOPORS and clustered in amino acid residues 807 to 867 (46/47, 97.9%).

evidence.reference_title: Mutations of TOPORS identified in families with retinitis pigmentosa.
evidence.snippet: A comprehensive analysis showed that 64.1% (25/39) of the mutant alleles are truncated mutations, and 34.3% (12/39) are missense mutations.

genetic_context.description: Functional impact is left unset because the literature disagrees between haploinsufficiency and a dominant-negative effect; see mechanistic_hypotheses.

nodes.description: TOPORS is a RING domain protein with ubiquitin and SUMO1 E3 ligase activity and is part of the ubiquitin-proteasome system; it binds the proteasome ATPase subunit PSMC1. In photoreceptors it localises mainly to the basal body of the connecting cilium, and to the centrosome in cultured cells. Which ligase substrates matter at the basal body is not known.
